name: etamil-support
description: eTamil, the Tamil-vocabulary FinTech DSL — with the compiler, the nUlakam standard library and the eTamil font included. Syntax, completions, hover, Go to Definition and errors as you type.
//license: AGPL-3.0-or-later, matching the repository's LICENSE. This said MIT until 0.3.0, which contradicted the compiler it ships alongside; the AGPL choice is deliberate and explained in the root README.
//icon: 512x512, the same mark as etamil.in. Without one the Marketplace shows a grey placeholder.
//capabilities: The extension runs a compiler binary and reads etamil.compilerPath, so it must not be active in a workspace the user has not trusted.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: eTamil runs the compiler to report errors, so it needs a trusted workspace.

virtualWorkspaces.description: Syntax, completions and hover work anywhere. Error checking needs the compiler on a real filesystem.

//activationEvents: onLanguage only. The previous version also used onStartupFinished, so it activated in every window whether or not any eTamil file was open, and immediately offered to run an install command.

languages.//icon: The file icon for .qmz, which is a separate thing from the extension's own icon. Without it every eTamil file draws the generic blank sheet. The same mark serves both themes: it carries its own dark ground, so it does not vanish into a light one.

etamil.compilerPath.markdownDescription:
Path to the `etamil` binary. Empty means use the compiler carried in this extension, falling back to `etamil` on the `PATH` when this build carries none for your platform.

Set it to run a compiler of your own — a `cargo build` of the repository, say. An explicit path always wins.

Machine-scoped on purpose: this names an executable the extension runs, so a workspace must not be able to set it.

etamil.eTamilFont.markdownDescription:
Font family for the ASCII that is **eTamil**, not English — `ceyal`, `moqqam`, the ezuqqu spellings in which one Latin letter stands for one Tamil letter. Empty, the default, draws everything in the editor font and changes nothing.

The editor keeps its ISO font as the base. Only eTamil-script ASCII is drawn in this face, so a name marked `_english`, a comment wrapped in `__ … __`, a string literal and the licence header all stay Latin. The rules are in `docs/reference/SCRIPT_RULES.md`.

The extension carries two. **`ican qamiz`** maps the 95 printable ASCII characters onto Tamil glyphs. **`ican qamiz Smart`** maps those, adds 72 characters of the Tamil block, and carries contextual rules: the pulli appears on a consonant that no vowel follows, a vowel that no consonant precedes is drawn full size on the baseline, and the inherent `a` draws nothing — so `vaNakkam` reads as வணக்கம். Those rules are asked for through `#etamil.eTamilFontFeatures#`.

Run **eTamil: Install the eTamil font** and it installs both, then offers to set this to `ican qamiz Smart`; VS Code has to be restarted afterwards, because the font list is read when the window starts.

A CSS font stack: `ican qamiz`, or `'ican qamiz', monospace`. Machine-scoped, and checked before use, because the value is interpolated into the decoration's CSS.

etamil.eTamilFontFeatures.markdownDescription:
OpenType features to ask the **eTamil** font for, where `#etamil.eTamilFont#` is set. Empty or `normal` asks for none.

A *smart* build of the font carries contextual rules in `calt`: the pulli appears on a consonant that no vowel follows, a vowel after a consonant shrinks to its sign, and the inherent `a` draws nothing, so `vaNakkam` is read as வணக்கம். The plain `ican qamiz` has no such rules and is unaffected by this setting.

These are declared on the eTamil spans themselves, not through `#editor.fontLigatures#`. That option is off by default and, while it is off, VS Code disables `calt` for every font; turning it on would change how every other file in the editor is drawn. This setting changes nothing outside eTamil-script ASCII.

A `font-feature-settings` value: quoted four-letter tags, each optionally followed by `on`, `off` or a number. Checked before use, because it is interpolated into the decoration's CSS.

etamil.checkOnType.description: Report errors as you type, using `etamil --check`. That mode stops after the type checker, so your program is never run.

etamil.intelliSense.description: Offer completions and signature help for keywords, builtins and the nUlakam standard library.

[etamil].//comment: Tamil renders poorly in most monospace faces, which have no Tamil glyphs at all and fall back mid-line. A stack that names Tamil faces first keeps a line of source visually even. It stays an ISO stack even for an author using the eTamil font: the base font is the one English has to be legible in, and etamil.eTamilFont paints the eTamil-script ASCII over the top of it.
[etamil].editor.fontFamily: 'Nirmala UI', 'Latha', 'Tamil Sangam MN', 'Noto Sans Tamil', Consolas, 'Courier New', monospace
